x.doc: The x position: a column, per-row values, or one value.

y.doc: The y position: a column, per-row values, or one value.

z.doc: The z position, in a 3D plot: a column, per-row values, or one value.

position.doc: Positions as one column or an N x 2 (or N x 3) array, instead of x, y and z.

fill.doc: The fill color: a CSS color, or a column of numbers or categories mapped to colors.

color.doc: The line or text color: a CSS color, or a column mapped to colors.

size.doc: The size of each point or label: a number, or a column mapped to sizes.

width.doc: The line width: a number, or a column mapped to widths.

opacity.doc: The opacity, 0 to 1: a number, or a column (categories map through opacityScale).

outlineColor.doc: The outline's color: a CSS color, or a column of categories mapped through outlineColorScale.

outlineOpacity.doc: Border opacity from 0 to 1: a number, numeric column, array or expression. Fades the border over the fill; mark opacity still applies to both. Missing values hide the border.

outlineWidth.doc: The outline's width in CSS pixels, drawn inside the mark's edge (a point's at most its radius).

fillScale.doc: The fill's scale, which marks can share: continuous({domain, colormap, transform}) for numbers, categorical({domain, range}) or ordinal() for categories.

colorScale.doc: A scale for color that marks can share.

colormap.doc: The colormap of a numeric fill or color: a name, a list of colors, or {colors, space, positions}.

sizeScale.doc: The size's scale, which marks can share: continuous({domain, range, transform}) for numbers (without a range, the automatic one), or categories with a numeric range.

widthScale.doc: A scale for width that marks can share, as sizeScale.

outlineColorScale.doc: A categorical() scale from the outlineColor column's categories to colors.

opacityScale.doc: A categorical() scale from the opacity column's categories to opacities, 0 to 1.

label.doc: The mark's name in the legend and the settings pane.

legend.doc: Whether the mark has a legend entry.

domains.doc: Whether the mark's data counts toward its axes' automatic domains; false leaves them to the other marks (a reference line, a decorative part).

rows.doc: "auto" draws one item when no channel reads a column (a line at a value, a label at a point), instead of one per row of the data; "@" view-state fields are not columns.

blend.doc: How the mark mixes with what is drawn under it; any mode but normal draws it transparent, and SVG and PDF exports draw additive and subtractive as an image.

glow.doc: How much the mark glows: its own color times glow blooms around it in the plot's presentation (0 does not glow); the Plot's bloom effect sets the bloom's strength and radius. SVG and PDF exports draw the whole plot as an image.

shade.doc: A plugin's shade (registerPlugin): { kind, ...parameters }, as { kind: "hatch", spacing: 6 } (Python hm.shade("hatch", spacing=6)), recolors each fragment the mark draws; picking, tooltips, domains and legends are unchanged. SVG and PDF exports draw a shaded mark as an image.

options.doc: The settings the settings pane shows for this mark, by name.

name.doc: The mark's name in the settings pane, and the name facet.endpoint() and partition.endpoint() find it by.

identity.doc: Whose rows these are for selections: an identity() shared by tables that show the same things.

select.doc: Click to replace the selection; an exact repeat clears it. Shift/Meta/Ctrl-click toggles membership (whole series for Line, Area): true uses its data's selection, or give a selection(). input("root").set("id") writes an input instead: a click sets it to the clicked row's id (a drill-down's root), .set(literal(v)) to a constant, .reset() to its default, and a click on nothing restores its default (input("root", {default}), else a Select of that name's, else null); several marks may write one input.

hover.doc: Mark the row under the pointer as @hovered (a whole series for Line, Area), without fading the others: true uses its data's hover, or give a selection(). input("focus").set("series") writes an input instead: while the pointer is on a row the input shows its series (or .set(literal(v)), a constant), then its committed value again (a hover that would change this mark's own rows is an error).

tooltip.doc: Show the nearest row's values in a box by the pointer: true, a list of fields, or {fields, radius, content}.

brush.doc: Brush rows with Shift-drag (point marks; Line, Area brush whole series): true uses its data's brush, a selection() shares one, {selection, axis} picks the axes.

nearby.doc: Mark the rows near the pointer (point marks): true, a selection(), or {selection, radius, units, axis}.

nearest.doc: Mark the row a tooltip shows as @nearest, with or without the tooltip: under the pointer, else the nearest drawn row within radius pixels (a whole series for Line, Area): true, a selection(), or {selection, radius}.

respond.defaultText: the states it sets, except hover and nearest
respond.doc: Which interaction states fade this mark's other rows to selectionOpacity; "hovered" fades them while hovering, "nearest" while a row is nearest.

selectionOpacity.doc: The opacity of the rows outside the selection while one is active.

drag.doc: Drag rows to move them (point marks): true along every numeric axis, or the axes to move along.

onclick.doc: Called for click on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

ondblclick.doc: Called for dblclick on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

oncontextmenu.doc: Called for contextmenu on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

onpointerenter.doc: Called for pointerenter on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

onpointerleave.doc: Called for pointerleave on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

onpointermove.doc: Called for pointermove on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

onpointerdown.doc: Called for pointerdown on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

onpointerup.doc: Called for pointerup on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

onpointercancel.doc: Called for pointercancel on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

onpointerover.doc: Called for pointerover on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

onpointerout.doc: Called for pointerout on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

onpointermissed.doc: Called for pointermissed on this mark; row provenance is optional after transforms.

ondrag.doc: Called while rows are dragged, each time they move. Python: on_event("drag").

ondragend.doc: Called when a drag ends; event.cancelled when Escape put the rows back. Python: on_event("dragend").

enterEffect.doc: How rows that arrive in a keyed update appear: "fade", or {effect, duration, easing}. animate()'s enter option is the value a channel starts from.

exitEffect.doc: How rows that leave in a keyed update disappear, as enterEffect. animate()'s exit option is the value a channel ends at.

animation.doc: Animate changes to the mark's values.

animationDuration.doc: How long an animated change takes.

series.doc: Split the rows into separate paths, one per value of this column (Line, Area). Without it, a Line colored or an Area filled by a category column splits by that column.

start.doc: Where each segment starts (Segments, Arrows): a column of positions or an N x 2 (N x 3) array.

end.doc: Where each segment ends, as start.

sampling.doc: Which rows a Line keeps when it has more than maxInstances: a random sample, or the extremes across even steps of x.

maxInstances.doc: The most rows drawn; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all), though SVG and PDF exports draw every row.

interpolation.doc: How a path between two points runs on a map or a globe: along a great circle, straight in longitude and latitude, or straight in space.

shape.doc: The point symbol: a shape name, a column of categories mapped to shapes, or one name per row.

shapeScale.doc: A categorical() scale from the shape column's categories to shape names.

sizeUnits.doc: What size measures: CSS pixels whatever the zoom, or units of the x axis, so zooming scales the points.

textureResolution.doc: The size of the texture a Heatmap's child marks are drawn into.

legendFontSize.defaultText: the theme's (14 in the default theme)
legendFontSize.doc: The size of the mark's legend text.

legendFontFamily.doc: The font of the mark's legend text, a CSS font-family.

legendTextColor.doc: The color of the mark's legend text.

legendTickFormat.doc: How a colorbar labels numbers: a d3-format string, or a %-pattern for dates.

quantize.doc: Step a numeric fill or color into `levels` colors instead of a smooth gradient.

levels.doc: How many colors quantize steps through.

maxElements.doc: The most rows the mark prepares on the GPU.

xTransform.doc: This mark's own x transform, instead of its frame's.

xbounds.doc: The x extent this mark maps, instead of its frame's domain (an image's or a grid's extent).

xrange.doc: Where this mark's x extent lands, in its frame's world units.

yTransform.doc: This mark's own y transform, instead of its frame's.

ybounds.doc: The y extent this mark maps, instead of its frame's domain (an image's or a grid's extent).

yrange.doc: Where this mark's y extent lands, in its frame's world units.

zTransform.doc: This mark's own z transform, instead of its frame's.

zbounds.doc: The z extent this mark maps, instead of its frame's domain (an image's or a grid's extent).

zrange.doc: Where this mark's z extent lands, in its frame's world units.

detail.doc: How finely a point's or a surface's geometry is divided (sphere segments, grid cells).

lit.doc: Shade the mark with the plot's lights.

transparent.doc: Draw the mark in the transparent pass, blended in depth order with other transparent marks.

sizeAttenuation.doc: Shrink far points in perspective, as three.js does.

zScale.doc: How high a surface's values stand: the relief's height scale.

surfaceMode.doc: Draw the grid as a surface whose height is its values, instead of a flat raster.

surface3d.doc: Draw the surface in 3D, lit and seen from the camera, rather than flat in 2D.

depthtest.doc: Hide the parts of the surface behind other geometry.

align.doc: How each text sits at its position.

billboard.doc: Turn the text to face the camera.

axisFontSize.defaultText: the theme's (14 in the default theme)
axisFontSize.doc: The size of the axis labels.

axisFontFamily.doc: The axis labels' font, a CSS font-family.

axisLineWidth.defaultText: the theme's (1 in the default theme)
axisLineWidth.doc: The width of the axis lines and ticks.

axisTickSize.defaultText: the theme's (3 in the default theme)

axisMarginLeft.doc: The space left of the plot area: "auto" fits the y axis's labels and title, a number pins it.

axisMarginRight.doc: The space right of the plot area: "auto" fits what reaches past it (the last x label), a number pins it.

axisMarginTop.doc: The space above the plot area: "auto" fits what reaches past it (the top y label), a number pins it.

axisMarginBottom.doc: The space below the plot area: "auto" fits the x axis's labels and title, a number pins it.

missingColor.defaultText: the fill scale's missing, else the theme's (#92989f in the default theme)
missingColor.doc: The color of the features the data has no value for: no joined row, or a missing (NaN) value.

Html.summary: Anchor ordinary HTML at a numeric 2D frame position; excluded from plot exports.

x.doc: Scalar x coordinate in the enclosing frame.

y.doc: Scalar y coordinate in the enclosing frame.

Plot.summary: A chart: axes, a camera and the marks inside it, in 2D or 3D.

animationGroup.doc: Match animation rows by these columns within each filtered/transformed snapshot; selections keep Data.key. null restores key/position matching.

description.doc: Your description of the plot for screen readers and exports; the generated summary of its marks, axes and legend follows it unless describe is false.

describe.doc: Add the generated summary of the plot's marks, axes and legend to its description.

tooltip.doc: The tooltip of every mark in the plot that sets none: true, a list of fields, or {fields, radius, content, mode}. mode "x" lists every series' value at the pointer's x in one box.

nearest.doc: The nearest of every mark in the plot that has rows and sets none: true, a selection(), or {selection, radius}.

loading.doc: "atomic" shows the plot once its first frame is complete; "progressive" draws each mark as soon as it is ready.

background.defaultText: the theme's (white in the default theme)
background.doc: The plot's background: a CSS color, or "transparent".

data.doc: A table or live pipeline output for the marks in the plot; the same as wrapping them in Data.

schema.doc: Column types for data, such as {"day": "datetime"}, as on Data.

key.doc: The column, or columns, that identify each row of data across updates, as on Data.

x.doc: The x axis: its domain, transform, label, ticks, grid and the rest of an axis definition.

z.doc: The z axis of a 3D plot, as x.

scaleDefaults.doc: Defaults for the continuous color, size and width scales the plot's marks make for numeric columns: each {colormap, range, transform, ...}.

zScale.doc: The height scale of every surface in the plot (a Heatmap with surfaceMode), unless the surface sets its own.

legend.defaultText: a legend at the bottom for each fill, color or outline color mapped from a category column
legend.doc: true shows a legend that explains everything the plot's marks map from data (a guide per channel, as a Legend without a channel does), then lists the labeled marks; {position} puts it at the "top", "right", "bottom" (the default) or "left"; false shows none. A channel an explicit Legend explains is left out.

coordinates.doc: The coordinate system: polar reads x as angle and y as radius; spherical reads x and y as longitude and latitude.

polarAxis.doc: The axis a 3D polar plot turns around; a 2D polar plot uses "Z".

sphericalView.doc: How a 3D spherical plot shows the sphere: as a globe, or flat in its map projection.

cameraMode.doc: How the viewer moves a 3D camera: "orbit" turns around a target; "flyover" moves like a map (drag pans the ground, the wheel zooms toward the pointer, right-drag looks, WASD and QE fly).

cameraPosition.doc: Where the 3D camera is; the plot's box spans -50 to 50. A new value moves it there (easing with animation).

cameraTarget.doc: The point the 3D camera looks at.

cameraUp.doc: The 3D camera's up direction, overriding the view preset.

cameraFov.doc: The 3D camera's vertical field of view.

flySpeed.doc: A multiplier on flyover's wheel zoom and key travel, from 0.1 to 10.

flyoverMomentum.doc: A flyover ground drag released while moving glides on for a moment, slowing to a stop; false stops the view on release, as reduced motion does.

lights.doc: Lights for lit marks: ambient, directional, hemisphere or point. Positions use world units; omitted, no lights are added.

effects.doc: Effects over the whole plot: {kind: "sky", ...} (a 3D plot's sky), {kind: "bloom", strength, radius} (how glowing marks bloom), {kind: "fog", near, far, color} (a 3D plot's distance fog) or a registered plugin's kind with its parameters. A kind no plugin registers is skipped with a warning. SVG and PDF exports draw the whole plot as an image while one shows.

oncamerachange.doc: Called at most once per frame after the 3D camera moves, with its position, target, up, fov, near, far, zoom and mode. Python: on_event("camerachange").

globeBackground.doc: A color fills the sphere under a 3D globe's marks; false leaves it empty.

angleUnit.doc: The unit of polar and spherical angles: "extent" makes the x domain one turn, "custom" uses anglePeriod.

anglePeriod.doc: Angle units in one turn when angleUnit is "custom" (24 for hours).

baseRadius.doc: The radius at zero: a polar plot's radius is baseRadius + radialScale × y, a globe's baseRadius + radialScale × height.

radialScale.doc: The radius per unit of y in a polar plot, or of height on a globe (see baseRadius).

projection.doc: The map projection of a 2D spherical plot (or a projected 3D one). An orthographic globe drags to turn; equal-earth, natural-earth, albers and albers-usa have curved outlines and draw a graticule instead of edge axes.

projectionCenter.doc: The map's center [longitude, latitude], in angleUnit: the orthographic globe's starting view, and the central meridian of equal-earth, natural-earth and albers (its origin latitude too).

parallels.doc: The albers projection's two standard parallels, in angleUnit.

interpolation.doc: How the plot's paths run between two points on a map or a globe: along a great circle, straight in longitude and latitude, or straight in space. Marks can set their own.

subdivisionTolerance.doc: How far a curved line, band or outline may stray from its true shape before it is divided further.

zoomAxis.doc: Which axes the viewer's 2D zoom changes.

dynamicMargins.doc: Fit axis margins during navigation. False fits initially, then holds this plot's own margins during pan/zoom; size, font, style and data-domain changes refit. Aligned peers can still reserve space; longer labels may clip.

axisMarginZoom.doc: With axes shown, zooming over an axis's margin zooms that axis only.

overviewScale.doc: A multiplier on the marks' sizes in the overview.

overviewMaxInstances.doc: The most rows per mark the overview draws; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all).

axisFrame.doc: Draw a complete rectangular border in 2D Cartesian frames without duplicate ticks or labels.

axisMask.doc: Clip marks and picking to the rectangular 2D Cartesian axes interior, intersecting ancestor masks.

axes3d.doc: Enable Cartesian 3D guides: true uses theme defaults; an object selects box or triad style and xy/xz/yz grid planes.

aspect.doc: "equal" keeps one transformed data unit the same length on all Cartesian axes, including 3D; "auto" fills the plot. In 2D an explicit domain is kept: the plot area letterboxes instead of widening it. Polar and spherical plots are always equal.

overviewAxes.doc: Label the overview's axes: true for both, or {x, y} to choose.

rules.doc: Reference lines across the plot at x or y values, each with an optional label, color, width and dash.

bands.doc: Shaded spans of the x or y axis behind the marks and grid lines, labelled like rules.

viewport.doc: The 2D view: its center as a fraction of each axis's domain (x, y) and its zoom. With onviewportchange it controls the view or shares it between plots; with animation, a new value eases there.

onviewportchange.doc: Called when the viewer pans or zooms a 2D plot, with the new viewport. Python: on_event("viewportchange").

interactive.doc: Let the viewer pan and zoom a 2D plot or move a 3D camera, and Shift-drag to brush a mark with brush; false fixes the view, and a plain drag brushes. "brush": a plain drag brushes, Shift-drag pans and the wheel zooms.

name.doc: The plot's name in its settings and export panels, and its accessible name when it has no title.

width.doc: A fixed width; without one the plot fills its notebook cell or exported page (in a Facet, its cell). hm.export_png, export_svg and export_pdf, with no page to fill, draw it 800 px wide; a view's own export draws it as shown.

height.doc: The height of the whole plot: its title, caption and top or bottom legends take their room from it, and the drawing area the rest (at least a quarter of it).

responsive.doc: True fills the container even when width is set; false uses width or 800 px.

type.doc: A 2D plot, a Z-up 3D plot (3d), or a Y-up 3D plot (3d-y-up); cameraUp overrides either 3D preset; SVG and PDF exports draw a 3D plot's 2D marks as vectors sorted by depth, and its marks as one image when one has no vector form there (a 3D mark, a Heatmap).

settings.doc: showTrigger: false hides the settings and export buttons; showExport: false hides the export button and the menu's Export entry; menu: false leaves the browser's own context menu instead of the plot's; allowSharedDefaults: false leaves the shared defaults out of the settings pane. The plot's export and openSettings() methods work whatever these say.

toneMapping.doc: The three.js tone mapping the plot renders with: 0 (the default) keeps colors exact, so marks match their legends; 4 is ACES filmic, for a photographic look in lit 3D scenes.

toolbar.doc: Your own content, such as buttons, at the bottom of the plot's box.

overview.doc: Show an overview in the corner: a minimap of the whole domain in 2D, an orientation gadget in 3D; exports leave it out.

axes2d.defaultText: true for 2D Cartesian plots and 2D orthographic globes; false otherwise
axes2d.doc: Draw the 2D axes: lines, ticks, labels and titles; on a 2D orthographic globe, a graticule (every 15°) and the sphere's outline.

orientation3d.doc: Show an X/Y/Z orientation indicator in the lower left while a 3D plot is hovered.

axisTitles.doc: Draw the axis titles, in 2D and on the 3D box.

antialias.doc: On-screen antialiasing: 4x MSAA (msaa), hybrid 8x/16x sampling (ssaa8/ssaa16: 4x MSAA at 2x/4x the pixel count, then downsampling), SMAA, or off. Hybrid modes cost more GPU work. Exports always use 4x MSAA at their requested resolution.

autoBounds.defaultText: true when the plot has data (its own, an enclosing Data or a Facet); Python's Plot sends true
autoBounds.doc: Fit missing x, y and z domains to the plotted data; an explicit domain always wins.

animation.doc: Animate changes to the values of every mark in the plot (marks can set their own), and ease a new viewport or camera prop (position, target, up, fov, near, far) to its value, except under reduced motion; the viewer's press or wheel stops the move.

animationDuration.doc: How long animated changes take, including setCamera's with animate.

animateBounds.doc: Animate numeric axis domains and ranges independently of mark animation; structural changes and direction reversals snap.

boundsDuration.doc: Duration of scale transitions, independent of mark timing.

boundsEasing.doc: Easing of scale transitions, independent of mark timing.

title.doc: A title above the plot, part of it on screen and in its exports.

subtitle.doc: A line under the title, smaller and lighter.

caption.doc: A note under the plot, such as its source, smaller and lighter.

filename.doc: Save an export to this file when the plot's with block closes; the suffix picks PNG, SVG, PDF or HTML.

exportOptions.doc: Options for that export, such as scale for PNG or mode and width for SVG and PDF; needs filename.

Heatmap.summary: A grid of values drawn as colors, one cell per value.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

fill.doc: The values, one per cell, mapped to colors: a 2-D array (nested lists or a NumPy array in Python), or a variable of a grid table. A 2-D array's cell in row i and column j is centered at x = j, y = i (row 0 at the bottom), so the axes span -0.5 to n - 0.5, unless the plot sets the axis's domain.

pixelated.defaultText: true for a 2-D array of at most 64 cells along each side, without surfaceMode or contours in a 2D plot; false for a grid table
pixelated.doc: Draw each cell as a flat square of its value instead of blending it into its neighbors.

x.doc: Over a grid table, the dimension drawn along x.

y.doc: Over a grid table, the dimension drawn along y.

Points3D.summary: Solid spheres or cubes in a 3D plot, one per row.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

size.doc: The diameter of each sphere (a cube's side is half of it): a number, or a column mapped to sizes through sizeScale (its range in world units: continuous({ range: [2, 8] }) spans small to large spheres). A 3D plot's box is 100 world units across, so 4 is a twenty-fifth of it; a few hundred points read well at 2 to 6.

shape.doc: The solid drawn at every point.

fill.defaultText: the theme's Points fill (#3478c7 in the default theme)

detail.doc: How finely each sphere is divided, 0 to 4: 3 is 320 triangles a sphere, 1 (80) draws a large dataset faster.

depthWrite.doc: Write visible point fragments to the depth buffer with normal blending; false leaves depth testing and nearest-point picking unchanged. Other blend modes disable depth writes.

Points.summary: A scatter plot's symbols, one per row.

xOffset.doc: Moves each row along x in data units: on a categorical axis a band is one unit, so 0.25 is a quarter of the category's band (grouped bars, dodged points). A number or a column. dx moves by CSS pixels.

yOffset.doc: Moves each row along y in data units: on a categorical axis a band is one unit (side-by-side horizontal bars). A number or a column. dy moves by CSS pixels.

dx.doc: Moves each point right, or left when negative: a number, or a column (Dodge writes one).

dy.doc: Moves each point down, or up when negative: a number, or a column (Dodge writes one).

depthWrite.doc: Write visible point fragments to the depth buffer with normal blending; false leaves depth testing and nearest-point picking unchanged. Other blend modes disable depth writes.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

size.doc: Each point's diameter in CSS pixels (in x units with sizeUnits="data"): a number, or a column mapped through sizeScale (by default onto the automatic size range).

fill.defaultText: the theme's (#3478c7 in the default theme)
fill.doc: The fill color: a CSS color, or a column of numbers or categories mapped to colors. "transparent" draws a hollow point, its outline alone (outlineColor, outlineWidth); colors are otherwise opaque (use opacity).

Segments.summary: Line segments, one per row, each from its start to its end.

connections.doc: Draw between other marks instead of from start and end: connect(a, b, {key}) draws a segment for each matched key and pair of adjacent endpoints.

dash.doc: Draw the line dashed: true (4 px dashes and gaps), a dash length (gaps as long), or [dash, gap], measured along the drawn path.

curve.defaultText: "linear", or "cubic" when control points are given
curve.doc: How each segment runs from start to end: straight, in steps, as a tree link, or as a Bézier curve through its control points.

control1.doc: Each segment's first control point for a quadratic or cubic curve: a column of positions or an N x 2 (N x 3) array. Without curve, control points make the segments cubic.

control2.doc: Each segment's second control point for a cubic curve; left out of an automatic cubic, it is the segment's end.

cap.doc: "bar": a bar across both ends; "arrow": an arrowhead at the true end, following the curve.

capSize.doc: The length of the bars cap="bar" draws.

headLength.doc: The length of cap="arrow" heads, limited to the segment's length.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

color.defaultText: the theme's (#3478c7 in the default theme)

width.defaultText: the theme's (1 in the default theme)

Line.summary: A line through the rows in order: one path, or one per series.

connections.doc: Draw between other marks instead of from x and y: connect(a, b, {key}) draws one path per matched key through the endpoints in order.

dash.doc: Draw the line dashed: true (4 px dashes and gaps), a dash length (gaps as long), or [dash, gap], measured along the drawn path.

curve.doc: How the path runs between its points: straight, in steps, or smoothed.

curveAlpha.doc: How a catmull-rom curve bends: 0 uniform, 0.5 centripetal, 1 chordal.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

color.defaultText: the theme's (#3478c7 in the default theme)

width.defaultText: the theme's (2 in the default theme)

Surface.summary: A 3D surface over a grid of heights, or a triangle mesh.

height.doc: The heights as a grid: row j, column i is the height at (x[i], y[j]). Without x and y the grid spans -1 to 1 on both axes.

indices.doc: With position instead of height, a triangle mesh: three vertex indices per triangle.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

x.doc: With height, the x of each grid column.

y.doc: With height, the y of each grid row.

position.doc: With indices, the mesh's vertices: an N x 2 or N x 3 array.

fill.doc: The color: one CSS color, or values mapped through the colormap, a grid like height (one per vertex for a mesh).

Arrows3D.summary: Solid arrows, a tube and a cone, from start to end points, one per row.

connections.doc: Draw between endpoint marks instead of from start and end: connections={connect(before, after, {key: "id"})} draws one arrow per matched pair, from the earlier endpoint to the later one.

curve.doc: How each arrow runs from start to end: straight, in steps, as a link curve, or as a Bézier through control1 (and control2).

control1.doc: Each arrow's Bézier control point, an N x 2 or N x 3 array or a column: the one of a "quadratic" curve, the first of a "cubic" one.

control2.doc: Each arrow's second control point, for a "cubic" curve.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

color.defaultText: the theme's Arrows color (#3478c7 in the default theme)

width.doc: The shaft's thickness: a number, or a column mapped to widths. A Cartesian plot's box is 100 world units across; a map's or globe's world is its projection's (a flat map is 2π across).

Text3D.summary: One piece of text drawn as geometry in the plot, plain or TeX math.

text.doc: The text to draw. Text3D draws one label; use Text for a label per row.

tex.doc: Typeset the text as TeX math (with MathJax), such as \frac{1}{x^2+1}.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

position.doc: Where the text sits, [x, y] or [x, y, z]: its middle, or the end that align names.

size.doc: The text's size (its font size): one number.

color.defaultText: the theme's Text color (#252525 in the default theme)
color.doc: The text's color, a CSS color.

Image.summary: An image drawn from its pixels: grayscale, RGB or RGBA.

data.doc: The pixels, row 0 at the top: [height, width] (grayscale) or [height, width, 3 or 4] (RGB, RGBA), integers 0-255 or floats 0-1. Or an image file, which the browser decodes (RGB, or RGBA when some pixel is not opaque): a URL; in Python also a path, bytes or a PIL image; in JavaScript also a Blob, an ImageBitmap, or an image or canvas element.

pixelated.doc: Draw each pixel as a sharp square instead of blending it into its neighbors.

lit.doc: Shade the image with the plot's lights instead of showing its exact colors.

fill.doc: Over a grid table, the pixels' colors instead of data: a column of [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] rows, or {r, g, b, a} naming a column per channel. Integers are 0-255, floats 0-1.

x.doc: Over a grid table, the dimension drawn along x.

y.doc: Over a grid table, the dimension drawn along y.

Theme.summary: Fonts, colors and mark styles for everything inside it.

value.doc: The theme: a preset from themes (Python hm.themes), createTheme(...) (Python hm.create_theme), or a definition object. An inner theme changes only what it names.

Minimap.summary: A small overview of a plot's whole extent, with a rectangle to drag its view around (a 3D plot gets an orientation gadget).

axis.doc: The Frame whose axis settings (bounds, transform, format) the minimap's axis labels follow.

axes.doc: Whether the minimap labels its axes: true for both, or {x, y} for each.

displayScale.doc: A multiplier on the marks' sizes in the overview, relative to their sizes in the plot.

maxInstances.doc: The most rows of each mark the overview draws; past it the rows are sampled (null draws them all).

for.doc: The Plot the minimap shows and moves (Python target=).

Legend.summary: A key to a plot's marks, or to the colors, shapes or sizes one channel encodes.

for.defaultText: the Plot or Facet it is in
for.doc: What the legend explains: a plot, a facet grid, a mark or a list of marks (Python target=).

channel.doc: The channel to explain: categories draw swatches, numbers a colorbar (fill, color) or a ramp of sample sizes (size, width, opacity). Without it the legend explains every channel its marks map from data, then lists the labeled marks.

label.defaultText: the scale's label, else the mark's label, else the column's name
label.doc: The legend's title. With several guides (one per scale), each keeps its own title.

position.defaultText: right with a channel, else bottom
position.doc: The side of the plot the legend sits on; left and right stack its entries.

Area.summary: A filled area between two edges, with lower=0 by default.

x.doc: The x position of each row; the area joins the rows in order. A horizontal Area takes y instead.

y.doc: With orientation="horizontal", the y position of each row; lower and upper are on x.

lower.doc: The first edge, a number or value per row; default 0. The edges may cross.

upper.doc: The second edge, a number or value per row, in value-axis units.

orientation.doc: Whether the area spans y between lower and upper along x, or spans x along y.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

fill.defaultText: the theme's (#3478c7 in the default theme)

opacity.defaultText: the theme's (1 in the default theme)

Data.summary: A table whose columns the components inside it read by name.

animationGroup.doc: Match animation rows by these columns within each filtered/transformed snapshot; selections keep Data.key. null restores key/position matching.

value.doc: The table: columns, rows, typed arrays, an Arrow table or a GeoJSON FeatureCollection (Python also takes it as the first argument); or a transform (a Filter, Group, ...: its handle in Svelte, value=node in Python), whose live output the components inside read, computed once wherever it is drawn.

rows.doc: Number of rows instead of a table: an integer from 0 to 2147483647. Generate columns with row(), random() and Calculate; pass value or rows, not both.

key.doc: The column (or columns) whose values identify a row across updates, so selections and animations follow it.

schema.doc: Column types, when inference is not enough: numeric, categorical, ordinal, boolean, datetime, duration or geometry.

Provider.summary: A table loaded asynchronously, from a URL or a load function, for the components inside it.

source.doc: Loads the data: a function load(context), or {load, requestKey, id}; fetchJSON, fetchCSV, fetchArrow and fetchParquet build one.

url.doc: The address to fetch, instead of `source`, with {name} placeholders filled from params. In Svelte markup write it as a string expression: url={"/data/{year}.csv"}.

format.doc: How the fetched file is read: JSON rows, CSV, an Arrow IPC file, or Parquet read by byte ranges.

path.doc: For JSON, a dot path to the rows in the response, such as "data.items".

columns.doc: For Parquet, the columns to read; the others are never downloaded.

params.doc: The load's inputs, as plain JSON values that fill the url's placeholders; a change that makes a new request loads again.

key.doc: The column (or columns) that identify a row, as on Data, so selections follow rows across loads.

initial.doc: A table shown until the first load completes, so the components inside mount at once.

debounce.doc: How long a change of params waits for the next one before loading.

refreshInterval.doc: Loads again this long after the last load ended; it pauses while the page is hidden.

accumulate.doc: Merge each completed load into the table on screen instead of replacing it: with key, a re-sent row updates in place and new keys append; without, rows append in arrival order. {maxRows} keeps the newest rows. New params start a fresh table, and a url's {version} placeholder asks for rows since the result on screen.

refresh.doc: Each change of its value loads again with the same params (a Button's count works: refresh={input("reload")}).

snapshot.doc: Whether exported HTML embeds the last result and never fetches; false loads when the exported page opens.

name.doc: The provider's name in its status.

onload.doc: Called after each load that shows a new result, with {revision, rows, ms}. Python: on_event("load").

onerror.doc: Called when a load fails, with {error, revision}; the previous result stays. Python: on_event("error").

Interaction.summary: Names selections as columns ("@focus") that the filters and channels inside it read.

columns.doc: Column names, each starting with @ ("@focus"), mapped to the selection() they read: 1 on the selection's rows, 0 elsewhere.

Bin.summary: Counts the rows in each interval of x (a histogram), or in each cell of an x-y or x-y-z grid.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

x.doc: The values to bin along x; each bin's row gets x0 and x1 (its edges) and x (its center).

y.doc: The values to bin along y, for a 2D grid of bins; each bin gets y0, y1 and y.

z.doc: The values to bin along z, for a 3D grid of bins; each bin gets z0, z1 and z.

bins.doc: How many equal-width bins span the data, the edges themselves (Dates on a datetime axis), a rule that picks the count as numpy does, or an expression such as `power(count(col.x), 0.5)`; {x, y, z} sets each axis.

interval.defaultText: the interval axis ticks would use for `bins` bins
interval.doc: For a datetime column, the calendar interval each bin spans, such as "1 month", "1 week" or "6 hours" (weeks start on Sunday); {x, y, z} sets each axis.

tz.doc: The time zone of a datetime column's calendar bins: an IANA name, "UTC" or "Local"; {x, y, z} sets each axis.

mode.doc: "aggregate" gives one row per bin, with its count; "assign" keeps the input rows and adds each row's bin: binX (its index), binX0 and binX1 (its edges), and likewise for y and z.

sharedBins.doc: In a Facet, gives every cell the same edges, with a rule or expression resolved over all the cells' rows; false bins each cell on its own.

empty.doc: Show the bins no row falls in; false hides them.

normalization.doc: Gives a histogram's bars, binning x alone (or y alone): each bin also gets y0 (0), y1 and y (x0, x1 and x for bins along y) holding its rows' count, their share of all the rows ("proportion"), or that share divided by the bin's width ("density"), so one Rect x0="x0" x1="x1" y0="y0" y1="y1" draws either orientation.

columns.doc: Columns to compute over each bin's rows besides count, each a reduction expression as in Calculate: {mean_y: mean("y")}, Python {"mean_y": hm.mean("y")}. Every reduction reduces the bin's visible rows; an empty bin's column is missing.

as.doc: New names for the output columns, such as {count: "n", x0: "left"}.

weight.doc: A column, or one number per row, that scales each row's contribution to count(), sum(x) and mean(x) columns (other columns leave out rows of weight 0; with a column weight, a sum, mean or count inside a larger expression is an error). An interaction column such as "@brushed" counts only those rows, and every row while there are none.

Filter.summary: Keeps the rows that meet a condition, or the selected or brushed rows.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

inactive.doc: What a condition on a selection or brush keeps while nothing is selected or brushed: every row, or none.

where.type: string | expression | {field, op, value} | selection | array
where.doc: The rows to keep: an interaction column such as "@brushed", a comparison {field, op, value} (op eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, in or finite), a selection, an expression with one value per row such as `greater(col.x, mean(col.x))`, or a list of these that must all hold.

Sort.summary: Orders the rows by one or more columns, so a line connects them in that order.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

by.doc: The column or columns to sort by, the first first; rows that tie keep their order.

order.doc: Ascending or descending; missing values go last either way.

Normalize.summary: Rescales a column to z-scores, to 0 to 1, or relative to its sum, first value or maximum, over all rows or per group.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

method.doc: "deviation" gives z-scores (0 for a constant column), "extent" maps the minimum to 0 and the maximum to 1, and "sum", "first" and "max" divide by the column's sum, first value or maximum.

by.doc: Normalize within each group of these columns instead of over all the rows.

as.doc: The name of the normalized column it adds.

Shift.summary: Shift a numeric or datetime coordinate by a numeric or UTC calendar interval.

name.doc: Names this transform for handle updates.

field.doc: Numeric or datetime column to offset without reordering rows.

interval.doc: Coordinate offset, or a signed UTC calendar interval such as -1 year; numeric datetime offsets are milliseconds.

as.doc: Names for the shifted coordinate and unchanged copy.

Window.summary: A moving average (or other reduction) over each row and its neighbors.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

field.doc: The numeric column to reduce; windows run over the rows in their order, so Sort them first if they are not.

size.doc: How many rows each window spans; windows at the ends use the rows there are.

reduce.doc: What to compute over each window.

align.doc: Where each row sits in its window: at its end (the row and the ones before it), in its middle, or at its start.

by.doc: Window each group of these columns separately.

as.doc: The name of the column it adds.

Group.summary: One row per value (or combination of values) of the `by` columns, with the group's count, sums, means or other reductions.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

by.doc: The columns whose values form the groups, and bins or hexagons: bin("x", 20) (Python hm.bin("x", 20)) groups the rows by their bin of x and writes its edges and center, x0, x1 and x; hexbin("x", "y") groups them by hexagon and writes its center, x and y. The output keeps them, one row per group with a visible row, with a count column. Without by, one row of totals over the visible rows (a count of 0 when none is).

columns.doc: Columns to compute over each group's rows besides count, each a reduction expression as in Calculate: {mean_x: mean("x")}, Python {"mean_x": hm.mean("x")}. Every reduction (mean, sum, count, median, ...) reduces the group's visible rows; a column read outside one must be a key.

as.doc: New names for the output columns, such as {count: "n"}.

Hexbin.summary: Counts the points in each hexagon of a hexagonal grid over x and y.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

x.doc: The x values to bin; each hexagon's row gets x, its center's x.

y.doc: The y values to bin; each hexagon's row gets y, its center's y.

bins.doc: How many hexagons span the x extent (or the x of `bounds`).

radius.doc: The hexagons' radius, instead of the one bins gives. Each row's width and depth columns give a Prism with shape="hexagon" this size.

bounds.doc: A fixed grid: the hexagons covering these x and y ranges, one row per hexagon with the occupied ones shown, so filtering the input never changes the output's length. Points outside fall in no hexagon.

orientation.doc: Whether the hexagons point up or have flat tops; each row's rotation column (30 or 0 degrees) turns a Prism's hexagon to match.

sharedBins.doc: In a Facet, gives every cell the same hexagon grid; false sizes each cell's grid from its own rows.

columns.doc: Columns to compute over each hexagon's rows besides count, each a reduction expression as in Calculate: {mean_v: mean("v")}, Python {"mean_v": hm.mean("v")}. With bounds, a count, sum or mean of a column keeps the fixed grid; any other column groups the hexagons.

as.doc: New names for the output columns, such as {count: "n"}.

Stack.summary: Stacks values on one another, for stacked bars and areas, 100% stacks and streamgraphs.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

x.doc: The column whose values make the stacks: rows with the same x stack together; without it, every row is in one stack.

y.doc: The values to stack; each row gets y0 and y1, the bottom and top of its segment.

series.doc: The column naming each row's layer; within a stack, rows are ordered by series, then by row.

order.doc: The order of the series in each stack: "none" (their own), "appearance" (by where each peaks), "asc" or "desc" (by total), "insideOut" (the largest in the middle, for streamgraphs), "reverse", or a list of categories. Every order but "none" and "reverse" needs series.

offset.doc: Where each stack sits: "zero" stacks positive values up from 0 and negative ones down, "expand" scales each stack to span 0 to 1 (100% stacks), "center" centers it on 0, and "wiggle" makes a streamgraph (needs series). center and wiggle need non-negative values.

as.doc: New names for the y0 and y1 columns, such as {y0: "low", y1: "high"}.

Rect.summary: Rectangles given by their edges, one per row: bars, bins, tiles.

x0.doc: Each rectangle's left edge: a column, per-row values, or one number.

x1.doc: Each rectangle's right edge; a rectangle whose x1 is less than its x0 is not drawn.

y1.doc: Each rectangle's top edge; a rectangle whose y1 is less than its y0 is not drawn.

z0.doc: Each box's bottom in a 3D plot: with z1, the rectangles become solid boxes.

z1.doc: Each box's top in a 3D plot; give both z0 and z1, or neither.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

fill.defaultText: the theme's first palette color (#3478c7 in the default theme)

rotation.doc: Turns each rectangle about its center.

Prism.summary: 3D columns (boxes, triangular, hexagonal or round prisms), one per row, extruded along an axis.

xOffset.doc: Moves each row along x in data units: on a categorical axis a band is one unit, so 0.25 is a quarter of the category's band (grouped bars, dodged points). A number or a column. dx moves by CSS pixels.

yOffset.doc: Moves each row along y in data units: on a categorical axis a band is one unit (side-by-side horizontal bars). A number or a column. dy moves by CSS pixels.

x.doc: The center of each footprint on x: a column, per-row values, or one value (with axis="x", x0 and x1 instead).

y.doc: The center of each footprint on y (with axis="y", y0 and y1 instead).

z.doc: The center of each footprint on z, when axis is "x" or "y".

x0.doc: Where each prism starts along x, when axis is "x".

x1.doc: Where each prism ends along x, when axis is "x".

y0.doc: Where each prism starts along y, when axis is "y".

y1.doc: Where each prism ends along y, when axis is "y".

z0.doc: Where each prism starts along z: its base, with the default axis.

z1.doc: Where each prism ends along z: its top, with the default axis.

width.doc: The footprint's size along the first of the other two axes (x for the default axis): a number or a column.

depth.doc: The footprint's size along the second of the other two axes (y for the default axis): a number or a column.

rotation.doc: The footprint's turn about the extrusion axis: a number or a column.

axis.doc: The axis each prism extends along: z, from z0 to z1, or x (x0 to x1) or y (y0 to y1).

shape.doc: The footprint's shape, stretched to width by depth.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

fill.defaultText: the theme's first palette color (#3478c7 in the default theme)

Facet.summary: Small multiples: one cell per category, per field, or per pair of fields (a scatterplot matrix).

cacheSize.doc: How many offscreen cells stay mounted besides the visible ones; 0 keeps none.

layout.doc: In a Facet inside a Plot, how the cells divide the plot: "bands" along the split dimension (the other dimension is the Plot's), or "grid", each cell with its own x and y.

bandPadding.doc: The space between bands in the "bands" layout, as a fraction of a band.

data.doc: A table or live pipeline output for the cells; the same as wrapping the Facet in Data.

key.doc: The column, or columns, that identify each row of data across updates, as on Data.

name.doc: The grid's name in its settings pane.

settings.doc: showTrigger: false hides the grid's settings and export buttons; showExport: false hides its export button and its cells' Export menu entry; menu: false leaves the browser's own context menu on its cells.

row.doc: A categorical column: one row of cells per value.

column.doc: A categorical column: one column of cells per value.

wrap.doc: The most cells across before the grid wraps, when only one dimension splits the cells.

rowOrder.doc: The rows to show, in order: values of row (a numeric row column needs this), or fields with fields or pairs. Rows with other values are left out.

columnOrder.doc: The columns to show, in order, as rowOrder.

fields.doc: One cell per field, over the same rows: in each cell the column value is that field and field holds its name. A list lays the cells along columns; {row: [...]} stacks them.

pairs.doc: A scatterplot matrix: each cell's x and y are two of these fields; {x: [...], y: [...]} makes a rectangular one. It cannot combine with row, column or fields.

triangle.doc: With a list of pairs, the cells of the whole matrix or of its upper or lower triangle.

diagonal.doc: With pairs, whether to draw the cells that pair a field with itself.

as.doc: New names for the columns the cells alias ({value, field} with fields, {x, y} with pairs), when the table has columns of those names.

scales.doc: How the cells share axis domains: "shared", one per axis; "field", one per plotted column; "free-x", "free-y", "free-z" or "free", each cell its own.

resolve.doc: Whether each appearance scale is "shared" across the cells or "independent" in each.

link.doc: Pan and zoom the cells together along x, y or both; "grid" links x down each column and y along each row; "none" keeps each cell's own. "auto" links the axes the cells share (not free in scales), which the grid labels once, on its outer cells. A Facet inside a Plot shares its camera and takes "none" (or "auto").

legend.defaultText: the cells' legend around the grid (by default, a legend for each color mapped from a category column)
legend.doc: One legend for the whole grid, explaining what the marks map from data and listing the labeled marks: true or {position} shows it, false hides it even when the cells ask for one, "cell" gives each cell its own.

title.doc: A title above the grid, part of it on screen and in its exports.

subtitle.doc: A line under the title, smaller and lighter.

caption.doc: A note under the grid, such as its source, smaller and lighter.

filename.doc: Save an export to this file when the Facet's with block closes; the suffix picks PNG, SVG, PDF or HTML.

exportOptions.doc: Options for that export, such as scale for PNG or mode and width for SVG and PDF; needs filename.

schema.doc: Column types for data, such as {"day": "datetime"}, as on Data.

Partition.summary: Repeats its children once per group of rows, all in the same frame: one line, fit or density per group.

by.doc: The column, or columns, whose values split the rows into groups; the children repeat once per group, in the column's order. Rows missing a value form a last "(missing)" group.

limit.doc: The most groups Partition mounts; more is an error.

legendGroups.doc: One legend entry per group, labelled by its value, instead of one per mark.

name.doc: The partition's name in the settings pane, where each group's marks are listed under it.

Dodge.summary: Moves overlapping points apart, for a beeswarm, or lays out one unit per row in a grid, for a unit (waffle) chart.

mode.doc: "collision" offsets the points of one point mark so they do not overlap; "grid" lays out units in rows of `columns` cells: each unit gets x and y (its cell's center), x0, x1, y0 and y1.

columns.doc: In grid mode, how many cells each row of units has.

count.doc: In grid mode, how many units each row makes (whole numbers).

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

x.doc: The points' x column: with axis "y", their positions; with axis "x", groups whose points are laid out separately.

y.doc: The points' y column: with axis "x", their positions; with axis "y", groups whose points are laid out separately, such as one row per category.

axis.doc: The direction points move to clear each other: "x", "y", or "auto": across a categorical x (or a lone y), otherwise along y. The point mark inside takes the offsets itself.

as.doc: The name of the offset column, in pixels; a point mark may still give it as dy (or dx).

seed.doc: The random seed of the order in which points are placed.

InputContext.summary: A scope for inputs: everything inside it reads the inputs inside it by name (a Python Scene is one already).

TextInput.summary: Text edited by the viewer, updated on each keystroke.

placeholder.doc: A hint shown while the input is empty.

name.doc: The name readers use (input("name"), hm.input.name, or "$name" where a string names a column): an identifier, unique in its input context.

label.doc: The text shown beside the control.

ColorPicker.summary: An opaque RGB color selected with the browser color picker.

value.doc: A six-digit hexadecimal color; the value is lowercase #rrggbb.

name.doc: The name readers use (input("name"), hm.input.name, or "$name" where a string names a column): an identifier, unique in its input context.

label.doc: The text shown beside the control.

DateTimeInput.summary: A date and time edited in a chosen time zone, held as a Date or null.

value.doc: The initial instant; omitted or null leaves the input empty.

timezone.doc: The editing time zone: an IANA name, UTC, or Local.

name.doc: The name readers use (input("name"), hm.input.name, or "$name" where a string names a column): an identifier, unique in its input context.

label.doc: The text shown beside the control.

Slider.summary: A number, date or two-endpoint interval the viewer drags between min and max, read by name.

min.doc: The low end of the range: a number, a Date, or an expression such as min("x") over the data around the slider.

max.doc: The high end of the range: a number, a Date, or an expression such as max("x").

step.doc: The distance between values; over Dates, a calendar interval such as "1 month" (which lands on month starts) or milliseconds.

value.doc: The initial value, or [lower, upper] for two thumbs selecting an interval. Endpoints are sorted and clamped to min/max; an expression reads the data.

format.defaultText: a numeric step's decimals, else 4 significant digits (12,346); over Dates, by the step, as an axis labels them
format.doc: How the value is shown: a d3-format string such as ".2f", a %-pattern such as "%b %Y" over Dates, or (in JavaScript) a function.

timezone.defaultText: the zone of the datetime column min or max reads, else UTC
timezone.doc: Over Dates, the time zone its steps and labels are in: an IANA name, "UTC" or "Local".

name.doc: The name readers use (input("name"), hm.input.name, or "$name" where a string names a column): an identifier, unique in its input context.

label.doc: The text shown beside the control.

Checkbox.summary: True or false, set by the viewer and read by name.

value.doc: The value before the viewer sets it.

name.doc: The name readers use (input("name"), hm.input.name, or "$name" where a string names a column): an identifier, unique in its input context.

label.doc: The text shown beside the control.

Button.summary: Counts the viewer's presses, so a prop that acts on each change of its value (reset=, refresh=) acts on each press; with set, a press writes other inputs (back to the top of a drill-down).

value.doc: The count before the first press.

name.doc: The name readers use (input("name"), hm.input.name, or "$name" where a string names a column): an identifier, unique in its input context. Optional with set.

label.doc: The text shown beside the control (needed with set and no name).

set.doc: Inputs a press writes: input("root").reset() restores root's default, input("root").set(literal("all")) sets a constant; a list writes several.

Select.summary: One or several options, chosen by the viewer and read by name; a Select of column names picks what a channel plots.

options.doc: The choices: a list of values, labels and their values, or categories("field") or columnNames() read from the data around it.

multiple.doc: Allow several choices; the value is a list usable with is_in(column, input("name")).

value.type: string | number | boolean | Date | (string | number | boolean | Date)[]
value.defaultText: the first option, or an empty list when multiple
value.doc: The chosen value, or list of values when multiple is true.

name.doc: The name readers use (input("name"), hm.input.name, or "$name" where a string names a column): an identifier, unique in its input context.

label.doc: The text shown beside the control.

Playback.summary: A slider with play, pause and reset buttons that moves its value over time, read by name.

rate.doc: How fast play moves the value, in value units per second; over Dates, a calendar interval per second ("1 day") or milliseconds per second.

loop.doc: Wraps back to min at max instead of stopping.

autoplay.doc: Starts playing when it mounts, unless the viewer prefers reduced motion.

playing.doc: Plays (true) or pauses (false) it from code; Python has play() and pause().

reset.doc: Each change of its value returns it to its first value (a Button's count works); Python has reset().

min.doc: The low end of the range: a number, a Date, or an expression such as min("t") over the data around it.

max.doc: The high end of the range: a number, a Date, or an expression such as max("t").

step.doc: The distance between values: play moves one step every step/rate seconds, or every frame without one. Over Dates, a calendar interval such as "1 month" or milliseconds.

value.doc: The first value, where play starts and reset returns; an expression reads it from the data.

format.defaultText: a numeric step's decimals, else 4 significant digits (12,346); over Dates, by the step, as an axis labels them
format.doc: How the value is shown: a d3-format string such as ".2f", a %-pattern such as "%b %Y" over Dates, or (in JavaScript) a function.

timezone.defaultText: the zone of the datetime column min or max reads, else UTC
timezone.doc: Over Dates, the time zone its steps and labels are in: an IANA name, "UTC" or "Local".

name.doc: The name readers use (input("name"), hm.input.name, or "$name" where a string names a column): an identifier, unique in its input context.

label.doc: The text shown beside the control.

Simulate.summary: Per-row state, such as positions and velocities, stepped at a fixed interval for the marks inside it to draw.

name.doc: The simulation's name in its status.

initial.doc: Each state column's first value: a column name, a number, or an expression over the data's columns. Rows that arrive later start from it too.

update.doc: Each state column's next value, reading the previous step (prev("x"), Python hm.prev.x), the data's columns, the step ("@dt", Python hm.view.dt) and inputs. Every update reads the previous step, so their order does not matter.

step.doc: The simulated time one step advances; the state after n steps is the same at any frame rate.

maxSteps.doc: The most steps one frame takes, so a slow device runs behind real time instead of stalling.

stop.doc: Settles once no column in `columns` (default: the updated ones) changes by more than `tolerance` in a step, checked every `every` steps (default 30). New data, inputs, running or reset wake it.

running.doc: Plays or pauses the simulation; running={input("run")} lets a Checkbox do it. Under prefers-reduced-motion one that plays from the start waits until running changes, as a Playback's autoplay does.

reset.doc: Each change of its value starts again from `initial` (a Button's count works: reset={input("kick")}).

Interpolate.summary: Fills a regular grid from scattered samples, for a heatmap, contours or a smooth line.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

x.doc: The samples' x positions; the output's x column holds the grid's.

y.doc: The samples' y positions, for a 2D grid (the output's y column); without it the grid is 1D.

values.doc: The columns to interpolate onto the grid, each output under its own name; categorical ones take the nearest sample's value.

resolution.doc: How many grid points: a number, or [nx, ny] in 2D.

method.doc: "linear" (1D), "bilinear" (2D samples on a complete rectangular grid), "idw" (inverse-distance weighting of nearby samples) or "nearest"; "auto" picks linear in 1D, bilinear for a complete grid and idw otherwise.

bounds.doc: The grid's extent, as {x: [min, max], y: [min, max]}.

Slice.summary: Each entity's values at one time (or other coordinate), interpolated between its observations, or one slice of a grid table.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

field.doc: The column to slice along, such as time (on a grid table, one of its dimensions); in the output it holds `at`.

at.doc: Where to slice: each entity's values are interpolated between its observations on either side, and entities without one on each side are left out.

by.doc: The columns that identify an entity; the output has one row per entity.

values.defaultText: every column but field and by
values.doc: The columns to interpolate: numbers linearly, categories from the nearer observation.

Pivot.summary: A long table made wide: a row per group and a column per category of a field.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

field.doc: The categorical column whose categories become the output's columns, one each.

value.doc: A numeric reduction expression filling the cells, over each group's rows in each category: sum("value"), mean("value") or count(). A cell with no rows gets a missing value.

by.doc: The columns that group the rows: an output row per group, with its keys (one row without it).

as.doc: Names for the output columns, one per category of `field`, in its category order.

Fold.summary: A wide table made long: each row repeated once per chosen column, with that column's name and value.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

fields.doc: The numeric columns to fold: each row appears once per column, with the column's name in `key` and its value in `value`.

as.doc: New names for the output columns `key` and `value`.

Join.summary: Columns from a second table added to each row, matched by a key.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

data.doc: The second table, whose columns are added; a new table replans the join. Or a transform (a Group of the brushed rows, ...), joined live as its output changes.

on.doc: The key column both tables have, or several for a composite key.

leftOn.doc: Instead of `on`: this table's key columns.

rightOn.doc: Instead of `on`: the joined table's key columns, paired in order with `leftOn`.

how.doc: "left" keeps every row, with missing values where no key matches; "inner" hides the rows with no match.

fields.doc: The joined table's columns to add.

as.doc: New names for joined columns, by their names in the joined table ({region: "area"}).

Sample.summary: Keeps a random subset of the rows, a number or a fraction of them, in their original order or shuffled.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

size.defaultText: every row, up to 1000 (every row with order "random")

proportion.doc: The fraction of the rows to keep, 0 to 1, instead of size.

seed.doc: The random seed: the same seed picks the same rows in the same order.

order.doc: "data" keeps the sampled rows in their original order; "random" puts them in the seed's random order, so order="random" without a size shuffles every row.

Summary.summary: An estimate per group, the mean or median, with an interval around it: the numbers behind error bars.

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

field.doc: The numeric column summarized; the output also has its `count`, `standardDeviation` and `standardError`.

by.doc: The columns that group the rows: an output row per group, with its keys (one row without it).

estimate.doc: What the `estimate` column holds: each group's mean or median.

interval.doc: The `lower` and `upper` columns: one standard deviation or standard error either side of the mean, a normal confidence interval, or a bootstrap one (missing for "none"). Only a bootstrap takes the median.

confidence.doc: The confidence level of a normal or bootstrap interval, between 0 and 1.

samples.doc: How many resamples a bootstrap interval draws.

seed.doc: The bootstrap's random seed, an integer: the same seed gives the same interval.

as.doc: New names for the output columns.

Transform.summary: Run a registered transform or graph layout with its declared parameters.

kind.doc: The registered transform or layout kind.

params.doc: Parameter values keyed by the plugin's schema; Python also accepts them as keywords.

name.doc: Names the transform, including its copies in a Facet.

by.doc: Group input rows by these columns when the transform supports grouping.

as.doc: Rename output columns: an object mapping original names to published names.

Calculate.summary: New columns computed from expressions over the table's columns.

columns.doc: The new columns, a name mapped to an expression each, all computed from the incoming columns. Python passes each as a keyword: hm.Calculate(total=hm.col.a + hm.col.b).

name.doc: Names the transform, so a Facet's getTransform(name) reaches its copy in every cell.

Force.summary: A force-directed layout of a graph's nodes and edges, simulated live.

name.doc: Names the layout, so a Facet's settings and getTransform(name) reach it in every cell.

weight.doc: An edge column of nonnegative weights, each multiplying its link's spring strength.

dimensions.doc: Lays the graph out in two or three dimensions.

seed.doc: Seeds the random starting positions, so the same graph lays out the same way.

repulsion.doc: How strongly nodes push one another apart.

linkDistance.doc: The length each link's spring pulls toward.

springStrength.doc: How strongly each link pulls its ends toward linkDistance.

centering.doc: How strongly each node is pulled toward the origin.

velocityDecay.doc: The fraction of each node's velocity lost per tick, like friction.

alpha.doc: The simulation's heat, which scales every force and cools each tick; it starts at 1, so bind it to read it rather than set it.

alphaMin.doc: The layout stops once alpha cools below this.

alphaDecay.doc: The fraction of the way alpha moves toward alphaTarget each tick.

alphaTarget.doc: The alpha the layout cools toward; above alphaMin it keeps running.

forces.defaultText: charge, link, and x and y (z in 3D), from the options above
forces.doc: Named forces, as d3's (center, manyBody, link, collide, x, y, z, radial). An entry named like a default force updates it, one with a type replaces it, and null removes it.

fixed.doc: Holds nodes at coordinates from nodes-table columns, expressions or numbers (d3's fx, fy, fz); a non-finite value leaves that node free.

initial.doc: Starting coordinates from nodes-table columns, expressions or numbers; a non-finite value keeps that node's seeded start.

warmup.doc: Ticks run before the layout is first drawn, so it appears already settled.

running.doc: Plays (true) or pauses (false) the layout, which otherwise starts paused; a Checkbox's input can drive it.

reset.doc: Each change of its value restarts the layout from its starting positions; a Button's input can drive it.

reheat.doc: Each change of its value reheats the layout (alpha back to 1), so it moves again.

step.doc: Each change of its value pauses the layout and advances it one step.

release.doc: Each change of its value frees every pinned node.

GraphData.summary: A graph from edges, with nodes given or inferred from the edges' endpoints; ordinary transforms operate on the selected table.

nodes.doc: One row per node with unique IDs, including isolated nodes. Requires edges.

edges.doc: Edge rows whose source and target values identify nodes.

nodeKey.doc: The node ID column of nodes, exposed as the canonical id alias.

nodeFrom.doc: Which endpoint receives each edge row's reduce results.

reduce.doc: Node columns aggregated from the edge rows, mapped to {field, op}; nodes no edge reaches receive each reducer's empty result.

DAG.summary: A layered layout of a directed acyclic graph, with edges routed around the nodes.

orientation.doc: The direction the layers run, from sources to sinks.

nodeWidth.doc: Each node's width, which the layout keeps clear: a number, or a nodes-table column or expression.

nodeHeight.doc: Each node's height, which the layout keeps clear: a number, or a nodes-table column or expression.

nodeGap.doc: The space between neighboring nodes in a layer.

Pack.summary: A hierarchy drawn as nested circles, each leaf's area set by its value.

root.doc: The ID of the node whose subtree the layout divides: the hierarchy's root, or any node below it (a drill-down), or an input a Select or a click sets. Nodes outside its subtree stay rows of the nodes table, hidden; depth counts from it (0).

levels.doc: How many levels below root to show (1: its children only); root itself is then left out, as its area is the whole layout.

value.doc: Each leaf's nonnegative weight, which sets its circle's area: a nodes-table column or an expression over it. A parent holds the sum of its leaves.

width.doc: The width of the area the circles fill.

height.doc: The height of the area the circles fill.

Treemap.summary: A hierarchy drawn as nested rectangles, each leaf's area set by its value.

paddingOuter.doc: The gap between a parent's edges and its children.

tile.doc: How each rectangle is split among its children, by d3's tiling methods.

root.doc: The ID of the node whose subtree the layout divides: the hierarchy's root, or any node below it (a drill-down), or an input a Select or a click sets. Nodes outside its subtree stay rows of the nodes table, hidden; depth counts from it (0).

levels.doc: How many levels below root to show (1: its children only); root itself is then left out, as its area is the whole layout.

value.doc: Each leaf's nonnegative weight, which sets its rectangle's area: a nodes-table column or an expression over it. A parent holds the sum of its leaves.

width.doc: The width of the rectangle the layout divides.

height.doc: The height of the rectangle the layout divides.

padding.doc: The gap around and between rectangles, where paddingInner and paddingOuter do not set their own.

Sankey.summary: A flow diagram layout, with nodes in columns and links as thick as their values.

value.doc: The edge table's column of nonnegative flows, which set the links' thickness.

nodeWidth.doc: The thickness of each node's bar along the flow; the layout spans 0 to 1.

nodePadding.doc: The gap between neighboring nodes in a column; the layout spans 0 to 1.

iterations.doc: Relaxation passes that straighten the links.

align.doc: Which column each node takes: its depth from the sources (left), its distance to the sinks (right), beside its targets for a source (center), or left with every sink in the last column (justify).

Flow.summary: A Sankey's links drawn as bands, one per edge.

startLower.doc: Where one side of each band starts, at its source node: a column of positions, Sankey's startLower.

endLower.doc: Where that side ends, at the target node: a column of positions, Sankey's endLower.

startUpper.doc: Where the other side of each band starts: a column of positions, Sankey's startUpper.

endUpper.doc: Where the other side ends: a column of positions, Sankey's endUpper.

Routes.summary: A DAG's edges drawn along their routed paths, bends included.

dash.doc: Dashes the lines: true (4 px dashes and gaps), a dash length (gaps as long), or [dash, gap], measured along the drawn path.

curve.doc: How each piece of a route runs between its two points.

Nodes.summary: A graph's nodes, one row each, for the marks inside to draw.

drag.doc: Lets the viewer drag nodes with the pointer, in a Force layout.

Edges.summary: A graph layout's edges, one row each with start and end positions, for the marks inside to draw.

GeoJSON.summary: Maps of GeoJSON regions, lines and points, colored by their properties (choropleths) and optionally extruded.

data.doc: The shapes: a GeoJSON Geometry, Feature or FeatureCollection, in longitude and latitude on a map. Feature properties are columns for the channels.

geometry.doc: A geometry column of the enclosing data, instead of data: a FeatureCollection given as a Plot's or Data's table has one named "geometry".

featureKey.doc: The feature property that joins each feature to a row of the enclosing table, matched against dataKey; "$id" uses feature.id.

dataKey.doc: The column of the enclosing table matched against featureKey; each key may appear once.

height.doc: Each feature's extrusion: a number, or a property or column mapped through heightScale. Only polygons extrude, in 3D views.

heightScale.doc: A continuous() scale from heights to extrusions: its domain (by default [0, 1]) maps onto its range (by default [0, 1], nonnegative and increasing); heights outside the domain clamp. The map is linear: a transform, a midpoint or a "symmetric" domain is an error.

plane.doc: In a Cartesian 3D plot, "xz" lays the features on the horizontal ground plane and extrudes them upward.

fit.doc: On a 2D map, zoom to the features (a city's districts fill the plot, not a speck in a world map); a Plot's own viewport wins. False keeps the whole map.

onclick.doc: Called with the clicked feature: event.feature, event.featureIndex and, with a join, event.tableRowIndex. Python: on_click(callback).

fill.doc: The fill of regions and points: a CSS color, or a property or column mapped to colors. null (Python None) draws only lines and polygon boundaries, using color and width.

color.doc: The color of LineString features and, with fill=null, polygon boundaries: a CSS color, or a property or column mapped to colors.

size.doc: The size of Point features: a number, or a property or column mapped to sizes.

width.doc: The width of LineString features and, with fill=null, polygon boundaries: a number, or a property or column mapped to widths.

outlineColor.doc: The color of region and point outlines.

outlineWidth.doc: The width of region and point outlines; 0 draws none.

VectorTile.summary: A basemap of land, water, roads, buildings and place names from vector map tiles.

url.defaultText: VersaTiles' OpenStreetMap tiles, which need no key and are credited on the plot
url.doc: Where tiles load from: a URL template with {z}, {x} and {y}, or in JavaScript a function of {z, x, y}. In Svelte markup pass the template as a JavaScript string: url={"https://.../{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf"}.

tile.doc: One tile to load, [z, x, y]: its zoom, its column from the west and its row from the north.

tiles.doc: Several tiles to load (at most 16), each clipped to its own square.

bounds.doc: A box [west, south, east, north]: load every tile it touches at zoom (at most 16).

zoom.doc: The zoom at which bounds picks its tiles.

data.doc: Already decoded tiles to draw instead of loading any: a GeoJSON FeatureCollection whose features name their source layer in properties.layerName.

styles.doc: Per part (water, roads, buildings, places, ...): false hides it, or {fill, color, width, size, opacity, outlineColor, outlineWidth} changes its look over the scheme.

scheme.defaultText: the enclosing Theme's basemap colors (derived from its colors when it has none), else "default"
scheme.doc: The basemap's colors: a theme preset's name ("dark", "sea", ...), "default", or part styles as for styles.

sourceLayers.doc: Assign a tileset's source layers to parts, {layer: part}, or hide one with false, before the built-in rules.

clip.doc: End each tile's geometry at the tile's edge (tiles overlap by a buffer).

fit.doc: Frame the tiles when they change, in a 2D map.

origin.doc: Draw in a local plane instead of longitude and latitude: meters east and north of this [longitude, latitude], times unitsPerMeter. For Cartesian and 3D plots.

unitsPerMeter.doc: The plot units per meter in the local plane that origin sets.

plane.doc: In a Cartesian 3D plot, "xz" lays the tiles on the horizontal ground plane.

snapshot.doc: In an HTML export of a scene, embed the tiles on screen as tileData; false exports only the url, so the page loads its tiles when it opens.

live.doc: In a 2D view (a Cartesian plot, or a map in any projection, the globe included), and under a 3D flyover camera (with origin and plane="xz"), also load the tiles the camera shows as it moves. Needs opaque styles; not inside nested Frames.

minZoom.doc: The coarsest zoom live tiles load.

maxZoom.doc: The finest zoom live tiles load; zoomed in further, those tiles stretch.

zoomBias.doc: Live tile detail offset in zoom levels, between -4 and 4: +1 doubles linear detail at the same view scale or camera height; -1 uses coarser tiles. Zoom limits and the tile budget still apply.

attribution.defaultText: the default tiles' credit when there is no url, else none
attribution.doc: A credit line in the plot's lower-left corner, kept in every export (most tile licenses require one); false hides it.

tileData.doc: Embedded tiles instead of loading them: [{tile: [z, x, y], bytes}], bytes as base64 text or a Uint8Array (null for an empty tile). Exported pages carry their tiles this way.

extrudeBuildings.doc: Under a 3D flyover camera, stand the tiles' buildings up from their height tags (5 meters when missing) with flat roofs; false draws flat footprints. 2D maps are always flat.

name.doc: The name of its group of parts in the settings pane.

opacity.doc: A multiplier on every part's opacity; live tiles need 1.

onclick.doc: Called with a clicked feature of an area or line part: event.feature has the tile's tags and layerName. Python: on_click(callback).

onload.doc: Called after tiles load, with the tiles, the number of features decoded and the milliseconds taken.

onerror.doc: Called when a load fails, with the error and, for a live tile, the tile; the previous tiles stay on screen.

Marginals.summary: A scatter plot with a histogram of each of its columns along its top and right sides.

data.doc: A table or live pipeline output for the scatter and its histograms; the same as wrapping the Marginals in Data.

schema.doc: Column types for data, such as {"day": "datetime"}, as on Data.

key.doc: The column, or columns, that identify each row of data across updates, as on Data.
