x.doc: The column the scatter plots along x, binned by the histogram above it. Required.

y.doc: The column the scatter plots along y, binned by the histogram to its right. Required.

bins.doc: Both histograms' bins, as Histogram's bins: a count, edges, a rule or an expression.

height.doc: The height of the whole figure, at least 160: the histograms take a fifth of it (at least 48 px) across the scatter's side, and the scatter the rest.

viewport.doc: The scatter's 2D view, as a Plot's viewport; the histograms follow it on their axes.

onviewportchange.doc: Called when the viewer pans or zooms the scatter, with its new viewport. Python: on_event("viewportchange").

FocusContext.summary: A line chart over a strip of the whole series: dragging across the strip zooms the chart to that x interval.

data.doc: A table or live pipeline output for both views; the same as wrapping the FocusContext in Data.

schema.doc: Column types for data, such as {"day": "datetime"}, as on Data.

key.doc: The column, or columns, that identify each row of data across updates, as on Data.

x.doc: The column the lines plot along x: a drag across the strip below zooms the chart to an interval of it (its brush's bounds), and clearing the brush shows it all. Required.

y.doc: The column the lines plot along y. Required.

height.doc: The height of the whole figure, at least 160: the strip takes a fifth of it (at least 48 px), the chart the rest.

viewport.doc: The chart's 2D view, as a Plot's viewport.

onviewportchange.doc: Called when the viewer pans or zooms the chart, with its new viewport. Python: on_event("viewportchange").

Polygon.summary: Filled polygons from their vertices in order, one per series.

x.doc: Each vertex's x position, one row per vertex. Leave x and y out inside Contour (bands), Voronoi or Hull: Polygon then draws the shapes they make.

y.doc: Each vertex's y position, one row per vertex.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

series.doc: Groups the rows into polygons, each group's rows its vertices in order; without it, all the rows are one polygon.

fill.doc: The fill color: a CSS color, or a column mapped to colors (each polygon takes its first row's value).

Panels.summary: Stacks Plots over one shared x: one domain, panned and zoomed together, its axis drawn once under the stack.

x.doc: Settings for the shared x axis (label, format, domain, ...), under each Plot's own x settings. Only the last Plot draws the axis; the others show their data over the same domain.

TableView.summary: The rows of the data around it as an HTML table, live: a Group's groups, a Sort's top rows, a Filter's kept rows; omitted from image exports.

columns.doc: The columns, in order: names, or {field, label, format} with a header and a d3-format or %-pattern, as tooltip fields take.

limit.doc: How many rows to show; the rest are counted below the table. A Sort above it gives a top N.

select.doc: Click a row: true selects its source rows in the data's selection, or give a selection(); input("root").set("id") writes an input (.set(literal(v)) a constant, .reset() its default), and a second click on that row restores its default.

hover.doc: Hover a row: true marks its source rows @hovered, or give a selection(); input("focus").set("id") shows the row's id in an input while the pointer is on it.

name.doc: A name for the table (its element's data-name attribute).

Title.summary: A heading or note beside plots, drawn as text that stays text in SVG and PDF exports.

text.doc: The text: "\n" breaks a line and {$name} shows an input's value. Python takes it positionally: hm.Title("..."). A readout shows live values: a list of parts, strings and reductions over the Data around the Title (count(where="@brushed"), mean("fare")), or {value, format} with a d3-format string; in Python an f-string does it, hm.Title(f"Selected: {hm.count(where='@brushed'):,}"). A live value follows the data and its selections, written as tooltips write numbers, "—" when no row has one.

size.doc: "title", "subtitle" or "caption", sizes that follow the theme's text size, or pixels.

weight.doc: The font weight, as in CSS.

align.doc: Where the lines sit across the block.

wrap.doc: Wrap words at the block's width; false keeps each line whole.

name.doc: A name for the block (its element's data-name attribute).

Mapping.summary: Channels (x, y, fill, size, ...) that the marks inside it share.

name.doc: The Mapping's name in the settings pane; the marks inside do not take it.

Text.summary: Text labels at data positions, one per row.

xOffset.doc: Moves each row along x in data units: on a categorical axis a band is one unit, so 0.25 is a quarter of the category's band (grouped bars, dodged points). A number or a column. dx moves by CSS pixels.

yOffset.doc: Moves each row along y in data units: on a categorical axis a band is one unit (side-by-side horizontal bars). A number or a column. dy moves by CSS pixels.

text.doc: The text of each label: a column, one string for every label, or one value per row.

align.doc: Which part of each label is at its point: its left end, its center, or its right end; "auto" picks each row's from its dx: left of a label offset right of its point by more than 4 pixels, right of one offset left, else centered.

format.doc: How numbers in the text are written: a d3-format string (",.0f", ".1%", "$,.2f"; default the theme's numbers.format, else as tooltips write them: four significant digits, whole numbers exact, thousands grouped from 10,000), or a %-pattern for a datetime column ("%b %d"). A number computed on the GPU (a Group's count, a Calculate's mean) is written the same way, with no as_category. "axis": the text is an axis's view-state field ("@pointer_x", "@view_y_min", ...), shown as the axis's readout writes it, finer than its ticks, as Crosshair's readouts are; "@pointer" shows both of the pointer's, "x, y". On a band axis the pointer reads as its category; the view's edges are band positions.

dx.doc: Moves each label right of its point, or left when negative.

dy.doc: Moves each label down from its point, or up when negative.

box.type: boolean | {fill, outlineColor, outlineWidth, padding, radius, opacity}
box.doc: A box behind each label: true for a white box with a gray outline, or its settings.

leader.doc: With an offset, a line from near each point to its label: true for a 1.5 px line in the text's color, or its color and width.

data.doc: A table for this mark alone: a mark with data displays on its own, in a Plot of its own.

size.defaultText: the theme's font size (14 in the default theme)
size.doc: The font size: a number, or a column mapped to sizes.

Anchor.summary: An invisible position that connections from a Line, Segments or Arrows attach to.

x.doc: The x position of each row: a column, per-row values, or one value.

y.doc: The y position of each row: a column, per-row values, or one value.

z.doc: The z position, in a 3D plot: a column, per-row values, or one value.

position.doc: Positions as one column or an N x 2 (or N x 3) array, instead of x, y and z.

name.doc: The name facet.endpoint() and partition.endpoint() select this Anchor by when a Facet or Partition repeats it (Python can pass the Anchor itself); also its label in the settings pane.

identity.doc: Whose rows these are: connect() without a key matches the rows of endpoints that share an identity().

enterEffect.doc: In a keyed update, arriving rows start from their channels' animate(..., {enter}) values; an Anchor draws nothing, so "fade" only sets the timing.

exitEffect.doc: In a keyed update, leaving rows stay in place, and connectable, until the transition ends.

animation.doc: Animate changes to the positions, so what is connected to the Anchor moves smoothly.

animationDuration.doc: How long an animated change takes.

data.doc: A table for this Anchor alone; unlike other marks, an Anchor with data still goes inside a Plot.

Tree.summary: A rooted tree layout of an edge table, as a tidy tree, an icicle or a dendrogram.

root.doc: The starting node's ID, or a scalar reduction over node columns and selection. Its depth is zero; every mode keeps only reachable nodes.

directed.doc: Follows edges only from source to target, instead of both ways, in every mode.

orientation.doc: The direction the tree grows from its root.

siblingSpacing.doc: The distance between neighboring leaves, across the tree (tidy and cluster modes).

depthSpacing.doc: The distance between levels, along the tree (tidy and cluster modes).

mode.doc: A compact CPU tidy tree, a GPU approximation reserving subtree intervals (tidy-approx), a GPU icicle of nested rectangles with x0, x1, y0 and y1 (partition), or a dendrogram with every leaf on one level (cluster). Every mode gives the leaves an order column, their place from left to right.

layerHeight.doc: Partition mode: nonnegative band thickness per node. Children start at their parent's end; zero collapses a layer. tween() runs before layout.

nodeWidth.doc: Each node's width, as a number or a nodes-table column or expression. Partition and tidy modes allow zero widths for collapsing branches; incoming tween() is evaluated before geometry.

childAlign.doc: Partition mode with widthMode "fixed": where the children sit in a parent wider than they are.

widthMode.doc: Partition mode: a parent spans its children's total width (proportional), or at least its own nodeWidth (fixed).

visualMargin.doc: Partition mode: a gap between neighboring rectangles, inset from each node's bounds without moving its center.

height.doc: Cluster mode: a nodes-table column of merge heights, which places each node that far from the leaves, drawn to scale as scipy's dendrogram does.

edgeLength.doc: Tidy modes: nonnegative incoming edge lengths read from the edge table, accumulated along root paths and multiplied by depthSpacing.

where.doc: Node-table predicate; hidden nodes disconnect descendants. The root remains present. Layout entry/exit retains departing branches until they shrink.

enter.type: { nodeWidth?: number; layerHeight?: number; edgeLength?: number }
enter.doc: Starting numeric contributions for entering branches. Omitted endpoints are zero; initial mounting rests at the target.

exit.type: { nodeWidth?: number; layerHeight?: number; edgeLength?: number }
exit.doc: Departing branch contributions, reached before removal. Omitted endpoints are zero.

animationDuration.doc: Duration of layout-owned entry and exit; incoming tweens keep their own timing.

animationEasing.doc: Easing of layout-owned entry and exit.

name.doc: The layout's name in the status its handle reports.

Frame.summary: A coordinate frame inside a Plot: its own scales for some marks (a second y axis), or a small chart placed within its parent.

animationGroup.doc: Match animation rows by these columns within each filtered/transformed snapshot; selections keep Data.key. null restores key/position matching.

animateBounds.doc: Animate numeric domains and ranges independently of mark animation; structural changes and direction reversals snap.

boundsDuration.doc: Duration of scale transitions, independent of mark timing.

boundsEasing.doc: Easing of scale transitions, independent of mark timing.

axisFrame.doc: Draw a complete rectangular border in 2D Cartesian frames without duplicate ticks or labels.

axisMask.doc: Clip marks and picking to the rectangular 2D Cartesian axes interior, intersecting ancestor masks.

placement.doc: Anchors a fixed-size frame at a point of its parent: anchor in parent data coordinates, size in CSS pixels (2D) or world units (3D), and an optional rotation. "fit" centers it in a Cartesian parent's domain, across 90% of the parent's shorter side, and refits it as the parent's view changes. It cannot combine with ranges.

rules.doc: Reference lines in this frame's coordinates (a spoke or circle in a polar frame), as on Plot.

bands.doc: Shaded spans of this frame's x or y axis behind its marks, as on Plot.

coordinates.doc: This frame's coordinate system. A frame that changes its parent's needs x and y ranges or a placement.

sphericalView.doc: How a 3D spherical frame shows the sphere, as on Plot.

angleUnit.doc: The unit of this frame's polar or spherical angles, as on Plot.

anglePeriod.doc: Angle units in one turn when angleUnit is "custom", as on Plot.

baseRadius.doc: The radius at zero in a polar or spherical frame, as on Plot.

radialScale.doc: The radius per unit in a polar or spherical frame, as on Plot.

polarAxis.doc: The axis a 3D polar frame turns around, as on Plot.

projection.doc: The map projection of a spherical frame, as on Plot. A spherical frame with ranges must be a flat orthographic disk (radialScale 0).

projectionCenter.doc: The map's center [longitude, latitude], as on Plot.

parallels.doc: The albers projection's two standard parallels, as on Plot.

atmosphere.doc: A glow around a spherical frame's globe in a 3D plot: true, or a CSS color (default "#7fb2ff") and a thickness as a fraction of the radius (default 0.1). It is not picked and has no legend. SVG and PDF exports draw the whole plot as an image.

x.doc: Omit it to share the parent's x scale. A domain (or "auto") gives the frame its own; a range places the frame within its parent, in parent data coordinates, and fits the frame's own data unless a domain is given.

y.doc: The frame's y, as x: a domain with side "right" makes a second y axis.

z.doc: The frame's z in a 3D plot, as x.

scaleDefaults.doc: Defaults for the continuous color, size and width scales this frame's marks make, as on Plot.

name.doc: The frame's name in the settings pane.

autoBounds.doc: Fit the frame's missing domains to its marks' data; an explicit domain always wins.

Markdown.summary: Formatted text (emphasis, lists, tables, math) beside plots in a Python layout.

text.doc: The markdown: CommonMark with tables, task lists and $math$; {$name} shows an input's value. Python takes it positionally: hm.Markdown("...").

width.doc: The block's greatest width: pixels, or a CSS length.

fontSize.doc: The size of the body text; headings scale with it.

align.doc: Where the text sits across the block.

name.doc: A name for the block, in export reports and as its element's data-name.

Scene.summary: The root of a Python display: it holds plots, layouts and inputs and stacks its children top to bottom.

theme.doc: A theme for everything in the scene: a preset such as hm.themes.dark, hm.create_theme(...), or a definition dict.

Row.summary: Puts its children side by side.

minWidth.doc: The width each child starts from (with widths, the narrowest share's; the others start in proportion): with wrap on, a child moves to the next line rather than get narrower.

widths.doc: Each child's share of the row's width, in order: [3, 2] gives the first child three fifths and the second two fifths at every width (a child past the list takes 1).

wrap.doc: Move children to a new line when they no longer fit at min_width.

Column.summary: Stacks its children top to bottom.

LayoutGrid.summary: Lays its children out in rows of equal columns (Python hm.Grid).

columns.doc: How many columns of equal width.

LinkViews.summary: Makes 2D plots pan and zoom together, over one shared domain.

axes.doc: Which axes follow when one of the plots pans or zooms. The plots are given positionally: hm.LinkViews(first, second).

scales.doc: "shared" shows one domain on the linked axes, the union of the plots' domains (their data, or an explicit domain), so the same value lines up in each; "free" keeps each plot's own. A plot's explicit domain is kept either way.

Template.summary: A reusable pattern of components, built by a class or function, with a slot for the caller's children.

Slot.summary: Where a template's children go: hm.slot() marks the place in its build().
